akien_verbatim.said: so this is part of a feedback loop! then it should say that somewhere on it. it's a feedback loop for x. and we should do that for all feedback loops because this is just one example. if every intention creates feedback loops, we'll have a lot!
this CAN go at the end of sail. what? this is the other end of /chart. thats what it loops back to?

the_ruling: Every feedback loop SAYS SO, on the thing. 'It is a feedback loop for X.' Not just this one — all of them, because every intention creates feedback loops and there will be a lot of them.

the_finding_that_produced_it.what: build_inspector is not three components sharing a file — it is A LEG OF FOUR DIFFERENT FEEDBACK LOOPS, which is why it read as three jobs in a trenchcoat.

measured.J1_component_hygiene: 123 lines (7%) — charter_on_disk, proofs_exist, silent_device, state_is_projection. Judges A COMPONENT. This is the post-build inspector Akien actually asked for on 2026-07-27.
measured.J2_chart_packet_judges: 1035 lines (62%) — the six charted stages, two judges each, constrain through validate. Judges A /CHART PACKET. Appears NOWHERE in the charter's `what` or `why`; it shows up only in the `gates` field as a count of proof teeth. It grew without ever being named as part of what this component is.

the_open_loop_this_exposed: TODAY J2's FINDINGS GO TO THE WRONG END. They land in the same `findings` list as J1's, which becomes BuildGateRed at the PROVEME crossing, which surfaces to WHOEVER IS CROSSING — the builder. So the chart-quality loop fires correctly and then reports to the person who did not chart it. The loop is open, and NOTHING SAYS SO, because nothing on the artifact declares where it was supposed to close. This is the argument for addresses made concrete rather than by analogy: it is invisible reading build_inspector, and it only appears when you ask 'where does this feed back to' — a question the artifact had no place to answer.
cc_correction_on_the_record: CC said one turn earlier that J2 should MOVE INTO /chart. That is wrong and the error matters, because it would have been built. Moving it into /chart COLLAPSES THE LOOP INTO A POINT: /chart cannot grade its own packet at chart time, because no new information exists yet. The judges are worth something precisely because the build HAS SINCE HAPPENED, so 'did the chart survive contact' is answerable. THE TWO ENDS OF A FEEDBACK LOOP ARE SEPARATED IN TIME, or it is not feedback — it is a self-check. Akien caught it in one line ('this is the other end of /chart').

the_settled_shape.where_j1_goes: The end of /sail — Akien, pass 5: 'my idea was the build inspector was part of the build skill (sail)'. It fires where the building happens and persists the validation that becomes the pass.
the_settled_shape.where_j2_goes: ALSO the end of /sail — same firing point, DIFFERENT ADDRESS. It reports to /chart, not to the builder. What changes is not where it fires but who it reports to.
the_settled_shape.where_j3_goes: Not a filter at all — it IS the gate. Under held-workflow-belongs-to-the-author it stops being four bespoke functions reached from transitions.py's if-blocks and becomes rows in the one gate table. NOTE: J3 is the pass model already written, 374 lines of 'does this boat carry what this gate requires'.
the_settled_shape.a_loop_is: (WHERE IT FIRES, WHERE IT REPORTS). Both ends declared. A loop with only one end declared is OPEN — and open is a finding, measurable rather than a blank someone has to notice.

why_an_address_and_not_a_field: CC's read, argued rather than assumed. A fillable `feedback_loop_for: "..."` charter field is the same shape as `how_it_learns` — and that is exactly the shape that gets a plausible sentence typed into it, the hollow pass /sorted already has to police. Same argument as intention+why.json forcing the why through the FILENAME: structure, not a field someone can leave blank (force-the-why-structurally). A loop given its own address has TWO ENDS POINTING AT IT — the observer and the receiver — so 'declared but never closes' is checkable by a reader that does not have to understand either end. It also answers Akien's own 'we'll have a lot': you can ask SHOW ME EVERY LOOP AND WHETHER IT CLOSES, which cannot be asked of a sentence scattered across thirty charters.
the_probe_is_the_runtime_half: Same idea at two scales, and it lands on what Akien ruled EARLIER IN THE SAME CONVERSATION. The WATCHME state 'causes the creation of a probe... in order to send back feedback about the intention' — that IS a feedback loop declaration, and it is zero-or-more precisely because an intention makes a lot of them. The CHARTER declares the loop; the PROBE is how a loop reaches across a gateway, a time, or a future event to close. See held-workflow-belongs-to-the-author and tickets/watchme-emits-a-probe.
open_and_deliberately_unanswered: Whether the loop registry is a directory of loop artifacts, a table in the graph store, or compiled from the two ends the way intentions-congruency-lab is compiled. Not ruled; the compiled option is the one that cannot drift, which is the standing preference.
Whether 'reports to /chart' means a live delivery (mail to the shim) or a finding filed at an address /chart reads on its next firing. The event-not-poll preference points at the second.

CLAUDE.md's existing IOU — 'every component's charter answers how does this component learn' — is ADJACENT but NOT the same question. how_it_learns is inward (how do I get better); feedback_loop_for is outward (what do I regulate). build_inspector has the first and lacked the second, which is how four loops hid in one file. Whether they merge or stay two questions is unruled.
